owner_posts.post_text:
Smart Grocery Shopping: Your Secret Weapon for Better Health

Ever walked into a grocery store for "just milk" and walked out with a cart full of snacks but nothing for dinner? You aren’t alone. Dietician in Charni Road Mumbai, sees how the grocery store environment is designed to challenge our willpower.

Mastering the aisles is the first step toward mastering your health. My top Smart Grocery Buying Tips to help you shop with purpose by Nutrionist in Charni Road Mumbai Geetanjali Mengi.

1. The "Perimeter" Rule

Most whole, unprocessed foods live on the outer edges of the store—think fresh produce, lean proteins, and dairy. The inner aisles are usually where the highly processed "convenience" foods hide. Spend 80% of your time on the perimeter.

2. Never Shop Hungry

It’s a classic rule for a reason. When you shop on an empty stomach, your brain craves quick energy (sugar and refined carbs). Eat a small, protein-rich snack before you head out to keep your impulses in check.

3. Decode the Label

Don't be fooled by "Natural" or "Healthy" claims on the front. Flip the package over:

* Ingredients: Look for short lists with recognizable foods.
* Fiber & Protein: Aim for higher counts to keep you full.
* Added Sugars: Keep these as low as possible.

4. Frozen is Your Friend

Don't overlook the freezer section! Frozen fruits and vegetables are picked at peak ripeness and flash-frozen, locking in nutrients. They are often more affordable and won't spoil before you can use them.

Best Hydrating Foods to Keep Your Body Energised and Healthy
By Geetanjali Mengi, Registered Clinical Dietician Nutritionist in charni road mumbai

Staying hydrated is not only about drinking enough water—what you eat plays an equally important role. Many foods naturally contain high water content along with essential vitamins, minerals, and electrolytes that support overall health, digestion, and energy levels.

Fruits like watermelon, muskmelon, oranges, strawberries, and grapes are excellent hydrating options. With over 85–90% water content, they help replenish fluids while providing antioxidants and vitamin C, which support immunity and skin health. Coconut water is another natural hydrator, rich in potassium and ideal during hot weather or after physical activity.

Among vegetables, cucumber, bottle gourd (lauki), zucchini, tomatoes, lettuce, and spinach are hydration champions. These foods are light, cooling, and gentle on digestion, making them especially beneficial for people with acidity, kidney concerns, diabetes, or during recovery from illness.

Curd, buttermilk (chaas), soups, and broths also contribute significantly to daily fluid intake while supporting gut health. Including these foods regularly can help prevent fatigue, headaches, constipation, and dehydration-related cramps.

As a clinical dietician based in girgaon charni road , I recommend a balanced approach—combine water intake with hydrating foods tailored to your medical needs, lifestyle, and climate.

Why is weight loss so difficult with PCOS/PCOD?

If you have Polycystic Ovary Syndrome, weight loss isn’t just about eating less.

Many women with PCOS have insulin resistance, which can make it easier to gain weight and harder to lose it.

The solution isn’t crash dieting. A balanced nutrition plan, adequate protein, regular movement, and good sleep can all support sustainable PCOS weight loss.

Looking for a personalised approach to managing PCOS and weight?
📞 Call now to book a 1:1 consult with Dr. Reema: +91 83693 93349
Customising meal plans that achieve your goals 🎯and don’t make you feel like you’re on a “diet”

Many people with Hypothyroidism and Hashimoto’s thyroiditis start eating less and less to lose weight.

In reality, undereating often backfires:
• low energy
• increased cravings
• difficulty maintaining the diet long term

A balanced thyroid diet matters far more than extreme restriction.

Need tailored guidance for thyroid-related weight concerns?
📲 Get in touch on +91 83693 93349 to book a consultation.

Hormonal Imbalance is often driven by daily habits—not just “hormones.”

Most common triggers I see in practice:
• High-carb, low-protein meals → blood sugar spikes
• Skipping meals → worsens insulin resistance
• Poor sleep → affects cortisol & cravings

This is why many women struggle with:
	•	Weight gain
	•	PCOS/PCOD symptoms
	•	Fatigue & Intense cravings

👉 The right “hormonal balancing” diet focuses on stable blood sugar and structured meals.

☎️Call to book a in-person/video consultation for your personalised diet plan.

Nonalcoholic Fatty Liver Disease is now common—even in non-drinkers.

Many people search for: “fatty liver causes” or “fatty liver treatment”—but the root issue is often lifestyle-related

Why it happens:
• Excess sugar & refined carbs
• Weight gain & insulin resistance
• Sedentary lifestyle

What helps:
✔ Balanced, protein-rich diet
✔ Reduce sugar & processed foods
✔ Regular movement

👉 Early fatty liver is reversible with the right approach.

Diagnosed with fatty liver or abnormal liver reports?

👉 Low protein, high-carbohydrate meals

This further slows metabolism and increases fat storage.

To break your weight plateau, start with:
✔ Including protein in every meal
✔ Avoid long gaps between meals
✔ Focus on balanced nutrition—not just calorie cutting.

Many people start their day with just coffee and skip breakfast. But drinking coffee on an empty stomach can increase stomach acid and lead to acidity, bloating, and digestive discomfort.

Coffee stimulates acid production. Without food to buffer it, your stomach lining may get irritated — especially if you’re stressed or rushing in the morning.

What to do instead:
✔ Eat a small breakfast first (eggs, paneer, curd, or nuts)
✔ Have coffee after food, not before
✔ Include protein in your morning meal to stabilize digestion

A small change in your morning routine can make a big difference to your gut health and energy levels.

If you frequently experience acidity, bloating, or digestive discomfort, your eating habits may be the reason.
